In 8 of the 34 cells that the checker scores 1.000, both reviewers independently mark the content wrong, and across those 34 cells their mean sits at 0.56 of the scale. The score indexes conformance to a written specification rather than perceived quality. The human scores return the same five arms in the same ranking except that goose and Mingbird trade the top two places, and every pair of their bootstrap intervals overlaps. The suite is also ours, and the gaps reported here cannot be separated from authorship. What would separate suite fit from a genuine harness advantage is a task family written by someone with no stake in any of the five harnesses. No independent task family was available, though the released suite allows one to be added. Every task, fixture and scorer is released so that such a family can be placed beside this one. A ceiling follows from the same shallow checks: at 4.7B Mingbird and goose both reach 1.000 on eight of the eighteen tasks, so more than a third of the suite cannot separate them there.

Internal validity

Each harness ships its own prompt and tool surface, so the comparison is between products and a difference between two of them cannot be attributed to one design decision. The mechanism gradient is the only place where a single family of mechanisms is switched with everything else fixed. Each cell is a single run. The gradient’s full arm reruns the matrix’s Mingbird cell at the same rung: the two differ by 0.233, 0.229, 0.148 and 0.012 at 0.75B, 1.9B, 3.7B and 4.7B, and a second collection of the whole 3.7B gradient moves that rung by 0.066. An arm mean can therefore move by nearly a quarter between collections with the configuration unchanged, so a point difference smaller than that is not interpreted across collections, and every paired contrast is computed inside one collection. A rerun of 72 individual cells disagreed with the matrix on 29 of 67 comparable cells, but the median absolute difference is zero and the disagreement is bimodal: a task usually repeats its score exactly and occasionally lands a whole point away. Per-cell noise is carried by the paired task-level bootstrap, which widens each interval accordingly. The rungs were collected in sequence, so a size trend is confounded with calendar time. Within a rung the harness order alternates by task, which balances warm-up and drift across harnesses but not across rungs. Quantization is not constant: the two smallest Qwen tags ship at Q8_0 and the rest at Q4_K_M, so the change falls between 1.9B and 3.7B. Its direction is measured in Section 4.7 on one base model at four bit widths, and it is not a constant offset: the baseline loses more than the completion-controlling harness as precision falls from 6.50 to 4.85 bits. At 3.63 bits both produce at a fraction of their high-precision scores, and at 3.15 bits both collapse to near-zero scores, with pi reaching its budget in all eighteen cells while Mingbird finishes fourteen and produces nothing in three. A bit-width change across 1.9B therefore cannot be subtracted from a size comparison as a fixed quantity.

A cell that reaches its budget is scored zero under the deployment reading, so a slow but correct harness is penalized. The rescored reading replaces those zeros with the score of the archived working directory, and both readings are reported at every contrast. The rescored reading conditions on an outcome of the harness, because whether a cell produces anything is part of what the harness determines, so it describes where the scores come from and is not used to rank arms on its own.

One arm’s floor is a reply contract and not a graded capability gap. mini-swe-agent ends fifteen of eighteen cells at 0.75B and fifteen at 1.9B with its own RepeatedFormatError, and at 3.7B five of eighteen reach the wall budget instead. The five-arm span therefore measures what a harness whose contract a model cannot meet costs to deploy, as well as graded differences between harnesses that can meet theirs. The span without that arm is reported beside the raw span at every rung.

Cell exclusions

A ladder cell is excluded only when the harness binary failed to start, when the runner raised an exception before the agent’s first model call, or when the inference server returned a 5xx error during the cell. These are infrastructure failures and not agent outcomes, and the affected cell is re-run. Three of the 360 ladder cells meet the rule. The excluded cells are listed with their reasons in the analysis output, and the reported means are also given with the exclusions reversed there; the reversal moves the affected rung means by 0.013 and 0.023 and leaves every conclusion unchanged. Cells in which the agent ran and then crashed are not excluded. They are scored as failures.

External validity

The ladder and the gradient ran on one Windows 10 machine (an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v2, 48 GB of RAM, an NVIDIA RTX 5060 with 8 GB, and one Ollama 0.40.6 server), so the hardware is a workstation with a consumer GPU and not a laptop. All four rungs fit entirely in the 8 GB card at the study context. Four models cover the band where local deployment happens, but they are not a random sample of open-weight models, and the results need not transfer to larger models, other runtimes, or other task suites.

One asymmetry shapes the failure mix. The host is Windows, the workspace path contains a space, and the third-party harnesses invoke a Unix shell. Windows is a distinct agent environment with its own benchmark (Bonatti et al.,, 2024), and the mismatch here belongs to the environment rather than to the harnesses. A model that has learned Unix commands writes an unquoted path, and the shell answers “cd: too many arguments”: pi records that error in eleven of its eighteen cells at 0.75B, OpenCode in fifteen across the ladder, six at 0.75B and six at 3.7B, while neither Mingbird nor goose records it at any rung. Mingbird is the only arm that states the platform and the shell mapping in its prompt, and it is not immune to the mismatch: at 0.75B five of its eighteen transcripts mention a Unix-rooted path. The asymmetry is part of what the system is, so we do not remove it, and the small-end results should not be read as platform-independent. It is, however, measurable against the contrasts. Dropping every task on which the baseline never writes the unquoted path leaves the 0.75B gap to OpenCode at +0.494+0.494 [+0.228,+0.740][+0.228,+0.740] over eleven tasks against +0.546+0.546 over seventeen, and the 3.7B gap to OpenCode at +0.763+0.763 [+0.525,+0.954][+0.525,+0.954] over twelve against +0.762+0.762 over seventeen. Against pi the exclusion leaves +0.367+0.367 [−0.041,+0.714][-0.041,+0.714] over the seven tasks pi never fails this way, against +0.483+0.483 over seventeen. Seven tasks are too few to settle that pair. The mismatch is therefore part of what separates the arms at 0.75B and is not demonstrably its carrier: the gap to OpenCode survives the exclusion and the gap to pi is left unresolved rather than overturned.

We did not run a second benchmark. The benchmarks that are standard at this scale (τ2\tau^{2}-bench, GAIA) need a cloud user simulator or a judge model, which would add a second model and a second source of variance to a study whose point is to hold everything except the harness fixed.

Conclusion validity

Eighteen tasks per cell bound the precision of every contrast, and a null is read as smaller than the study could see. At 4.7B the observed contrast with goose, +0.250+0.250, sits just above that rung’s minimum detectable effect of 0.221 and is significant all the same, which is not a contradiction: the minimum detectable effect is the difference a study of this size detects four times in five, not a floor below which nothing can be found. The confirmatory family has seven tests and is corrected with Holm. The seven are not independent, since the four per-rung contrasts share tasks and arms and the three trend tests are computed from the same per-rung quantities. Holm holds under arbitrary dependence, so the sharing does not invalidate the correction. It makes the corrected values conservative when the tests move together, which they do here.

Experimenter bias

The authors wrote one of the five harnesses, the 18 tasks, the scorer and the analysis plan. Four things limit the room for that bias. The scorer reads artifacts and not the transcript. Every cell is recorded. Budgets and sampling are identical within a rung. The analysis plan and its multiplicity family were fixed before the confirmatory contrasts were read, as Section 3.8 records. The failure coding is mechanical, a file-existence test and the runner’s termination record, but it was not coded blind to harness identity because the directory names carry it. Every number can be recomputed from the per-cell results, and any harness can be rerun against the same suite.

7 Conclusion

Local agents on consumer hardware are usually discussed as a model problem. They are also a harness problem. This study compared five harnesses on 18 artifact-producing tasks against four open-weight models from 0.75B to 4.7B on one Windows host, with a 35.5B anchor at the top.

The completion-controlling harness had the highest mean at each of the four rungs. Two of the four pre-registered rung contrasts survive Holm correction and thirteen of sixteen paired comparisons exclude zero, with the leads that do run from 0.075 to 0.819. That ordering is what repeats. Three collections of the winner’s 0.75B cells average 0.664, 0.503 and 0.431, and in the two that also contain a baseline the paired gap against goose is +0.508+0.508 and +0.476+0.476.

The slope of that lead is a different question, and four rungs cannot answer it. The span slope is +0.198+0.198 [−0.078,+0.476][-0.078,+0.476], consistent with a fall of a tenth of a point per decade and with a rise of almost half a point. The three artifacts in Section 4.3 show why any answer would be an artifact of the estimator: a floor arm produces a rise, a ceiling a decline, a cross-family rung a peak.

The ablation contradicts the design story. The six executable completion checks, which are what the harness was built around, are worth 0.080 at 0.75B and 0.117 at 1.9B, with intervals that include zero, and nothing at the two large rungs. At the smallest rung the point estimate is a sixth of the lead. At 1.9B it is half, and there the checks are what turn three empty runs into finished ones. At the largest the interval bounds their share at 18%. The rest is a progress effect: the tool surface sends a directory listing through a shell that rejects the unquoted path, and the model then repeats the failing call until the context window fills. At 0.75B pi leaves nine empty cells and every one of them carries that shell error, and the same model completes the same task in Mingbird once the repeat is interrupted and the context reset. That rule is tested directly: removing it and nothing else costs 0.411 at 0.75B and turns eight of eighteen tasks from an artifact into an empty directory. The design still does not separate the tool surface from the rule, since the failing shell call that starts the loop is a consequence of the surface, and a tool-surface ablation inside one harness remains the next study.

Of 127 cells that produced none of their declared artifacts, 85 ended with a normal exit and 40 of those recorded no error line. A benchmark that read the exit status as the outcome would credit every one of them, and the fix is to score the artifact, not the process.

Three things would strengthen the design: a task suite written by someone with no stake in any of the five harnesses, a second host operating system, and repeated runs per cell. A fourth was measured here rather than assumed. Quantization is not a constant across the ladder, so Section 4.7 runs one base model at four bit widths and reports where the advantage survives compression and where it does not. Every cell, transcript, and score is available from the corresponding authors, so that a reader can attempt the three extensions this study could not run.

Every number in this paper is backed by one score file, transcript and working directory per cell, together with the analysis scripts and the digests of the served model artifacts. That archive is too large to carry as supplementary data and is available from the corresponding authors on request.

Declaration of generative AI in writing

Large language models were used to assist with code development, experiment orchestration, statistical analysis, and language editing. All technical claims, numbers, and interpretations were reviewed and verified by the authors, who take full responsibility for the work.

Appendix A The held-out task suite

The suite has eighteen tasks in four tiers. Each task is a working directory with fixtures, a prompt, a list of milestone checks, and a list of final deliverables. The prompt states the deliverable names and the checks that will be applied, and the fixtures contain the data the task is about. Nothing in the working directory tells the agent which harness it is running under.

Each task starts from a workflow that a practitioner described in public: screening a literature export, auditing a manuscript’s claims against its own tables, turning a CLI’s logs into a daily usage report, reproducing a published figure from the raw data, and so on. The task was then written so that completion is a property of the working directory: every check reads a named file and applies a rule that can be evaluated without a model. No task was written by looking at how any harness performed. The suite was frozen before the ladder ran and no task was edited afterwards.

Tier 1 asks for extraction from a fixture database. Tier 2 asks for synthesis across records, including disagreements between them. Tier 3 asks for a multi-step workflow with code, data products and a written deliverable. Tier 4 is long-horizon, with an intermediate deliverable that later steps consume and, in two of its three tasks, eight or more milestones. The tiers vary the length of the dependency chain rather than the domain difficulty, which is why the ladder is analyzed per task and not per tier.

Every check is binary. The milestone score is the mean of its checks, the final-artifact score is the mean of its checks, and the task score is

task=47​milestone+37​final.\text{task}=\tfrac{4}{7}\,\text{milestone}+\tfrac{3}{7}\,\text{final}.

The scorer also defines a third, judge-based dimension at weight 0.3. It is disabled in every reported run, which is why the two deterministic dimensions carry weights 4/7 and 3/7 rather than 0.4 and 0.3. A cell’s outcome is its task score, and a cell that reaches its wall budget scores zero regardless of what its working directory contains. HWF-01, for example, has two milestone checks and two final checks, so a cell that passes one milestone check and both final checks scores 47​(0.5)+37​(1.0)=0.714\tfrac{4}{7}(0.5)+\tfrac{3}{7}(1.0)=0.714.

More than half of the checks test presence or a substring (Table 12), so a score is best read as “the harness produced the specified files with plausible content” rather than “the work is correct”. The identifier-fidelity audit in Section 4.5 measures the part the checks cannot.

The tasks do not test conversational ability, tool selection under ambiguity, or recovery from a hostile user. They test whether an agent can turn fixtures into a specified set of files. That is a narrow construct, chosen deliberately so that the outcome can be checked deterministically at every cell.

Appendix B Reproducibility

The five harnesses (four third-party at the versions in Table 2, with Mingbird at release v3.1.9, commit 56cd23d), the 18 tasks with their fixtures (CC BY 4.0), the deterministic scorer and the runner that executes a cell are at https://github.com/Mingbird/Mingbird-agent, which also holds the earlier 288-cell matrix and the design-paper release. The scorer and the runner are code and carry the harness’s Apache-2.0 license, not the data license. The per-cell archive, one score file, transcript and working directory per cell, together with the sampling proxy and the analysis scripts, is described under Data availability.

Hardware and backend

The matrix ran on one Windows 10 machine: an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v2, 48 GB of RAM, and an NVIDIA RTX 5060 with 8 GB, served by Ollama 0.40.6 started as a dedicated process on port 11437 with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=32768 and OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1. A sampling proxy on port 11438 rewrites the temperature and the thinking field of every request from the harnesses that expose no such knob. The proxy logs each request, and that log is in the per-cell archive. That thinking is off is verified per rung rather than assumed: each probe sends one prompt through both proxy paths and once to the model with thinking forced on, and on every model the study loaded the two proxy paths return an answer of identical length while the forced-on control returns reasoning text and no answer. The records are in the per-cell archive as analysis/thinking_probe_*.json.

The loaded model’s size, processor split and context are recorded from the server’s /api/ps together with the pid that owned the port, at the end of every cell and, from 25 October on, at the start as well. The end-of-cell record reaches every reported cell except the first three.

The served window is verified per cell rather than assumed. The guard records the pid of the server it starts and evicts any other process holding the port, Mingbird carries its own context through AGENT_CTX, and the matrix driver refuses to start a cell against a runner whose window is off the protocol. An extraction of the server’s startup log is in the per-cell archive as engine_windows.json, one record per server start with the context pin it was launched under.

The precision ladder ran on a second host

The matrix, the gradient and the anchor ran on the host described above. The precision ladder of Section 4.7 ran on a second machine of the same class: an Intel Xeon E5-2696 v3 with 64 GB of RAM, the same RTX 5060 with 8 GB, and the same pinned Ollama build and protocol. Every (task, arm, level) triple inside a task ran on one machine in one contiguous window, so a platform difference cannot be recorded as an effect of bit width.

One-cell reproduction

Prepare a clean workdir from the task JSON and its fixtures, then run run_cell.py with the agent, task, model, timeout, run id, the two ports and the harness root as arguments. The runner writes score.json, transcript.txt and the working directory per cell, so a failed reproduction is inspectable at the same granularity as the published data. Rescoring a working directory with the scorer that ships at repo/bench/lrab/scoring/score_task.py, passing the task, the working directory and --no-judge, reproduces the published score exactly: every cell that carries both a score and a working directory was rescored this way and all of them matched, and the same procedure produced the rescored reading of Section 4.2 for the 58 timed-out cells. Three arms need a binary we cannot redistribute. pi is a Node package (@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 1.3.0) that the runner resolves through PI_CLI, then ~/myagents-bin/pi, then PATH. mini-swe-agent runs under a Python interpreter selected by AGENT_MINI_PY, and the shims in experiments/artifacts/bin point opencode at the 1.18.23 build.

Analysis scripts

analyze_paper_b.py computes means, gaps, trend tests and the minimum detectable effect. analyze_paper_b_gradient.py computes the mechanism gradient. classify_failures_paper_b.py does the two-axis failure coding. detect_loops_paper_b.py finds the longest identical action run per cell. grounding_audit.py measures identifier fidelity. check_discrimination.py reports which checks separate harnesses, and benchmark_validity.py computes task discrimination, split-half reliability and parallel-form transfer. rescore_timeouts.py produces the rescored reading, analyze_two_readings.py builds the per-rung quantities under both readings, and slope_intervals.py puts the task-bootstrap interval on every slope in Table 6. analyze_quant_axis.py computes the precision ladder’s level contrasts, its slope and its Holm family. audit_cells.py gates completeness against the 18×5×418\times 5\times 4 design, and print_paper_b_numbers.py prints every number quoted in this paper from the summary files, so a reader can regenerate the Results section without transcribing from a second source.

The analysis plan

The hypotheses, their estimators and their refutation criteria are set out in PREREGISTRATION_PAPERB.md, supplied with the per-cell archive and frozen on 22 October 2026.

The study build

Mingbird runs release v3.1.9 at commit 56cd23d. The three arms of the mechanism gradient are selected by the AGENT_ABLATION environment variable rather than by separate code branches: finish_gate disables the executable completion checks, and finish_gate_text_only disables those checks and the todo-sync reminder as well. The checks switched off are the no-work refusal, the test-not-green guard, the finish-claim artifact check, the plan-completeness gate, the artifact-content check, and the post-finish summary. The switch is the only difference between the arms: model, prompt, window, budgets, and the deterministic scorer are identical, and the switch ships with the code.
